beats.text: Siri was an app on the App Store before Apple owned it.
beats.note: It arrived as a third party app for the iPhone, from a company that had spun out of SRI.

beats.text: It grew out of a government funded AI project.
beats.note: MIT Technology Review says it was built on artificial intelligence research done at SRI as part of the CALO project.

beats.name: Dag Kittlaus
beats.role: Co-founder and chief executive of Siri. He told eWeek the app would reach Android and BlackBerry phones within months.

beats.text: Apple bought it within three months of launch.
beats.note: The deal surfaced in an FTC filing dated 27 April 2010. Xconomy later gave a reported price of US$150 million to US$250 million.

beats.text: Analysts did not expect Android or BlackBerry versions after the sale.
beats.note: eWeek thought it doubtful Siri would ever reach them. MIT Technology Review called a Siri for Android an unlikely prospect.

beats.text: Siri came back inside the iPhone 4S.
beats.note: Apple launched the phone with a beta version of Siri. After the announcement it removed the standalone app from the App Store.

beats.text: Once Apple built it into the iPhone, it pulled the original app.
